heading: Internal edits can recover knowledge after unlearning
definition: ablating an activation direction restores it; or analysis shows the method blocks access rather than deleting.
summary: Several independent groups recovered performance after RMU unlearning by removing a direction from the model's internal activations (activation-direction ablation), with results on Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Recovery depends on the method and model; broader evidence that unlearning blocks access to retained knowledge is mostly correlational.

suggested_status.by_scale: 1-10B: R2. Direction ablation on RMU was reproduced by different groups on Zephyr-7B (2409.18025, lw:6QYpXEscd8GuE7BgW) and on Llama-3-8B-Instruct (lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk). Several groups also report blocking-type internal evidence (2410.06606, 2608.11408, 2605.24614, 2601.15111). This scale has method-specific challenges: GradDiff, NPO-ILU, LUNAR's own attack, Gemma-2B toxicity, and probe nulls on RMU. 10-100B: R0. The only causal test is expert forcing on Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE (2601.16905). 2609.38909 is correlational only at 32B, and the original's Yi-34B RMU probes are null and figure-only. <1B: R0 for ablation (GPT-2 Medium RMU toxicity, 2602.23391). Toy and from-scratch settings from several groups (2602.19215, 2605.01699, 2609.27593, 2601.23153, 2504.05058) agree on retained structure under GA-type erasure, but not under distillation or with an unfrozen encoder. >100B: none (counts versions.C.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key). Non-LLM vision classifiers: retained class structure reported by several groups on ResNet-18 CIFAR-10, strongly method-dependent.
suggested_status.reason:
Ablation clause. Per-layer direction ablation restores Zephyr-7B RMU WMDP-Bio 29.9→64.7 (2409.18025, reviewed TMLR). A post by a different author recovers ~71% of the Bio gap on the same model (lw:6QYpXEscd8GuE7BgW). On a second family, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, RMU goes 28.0→53.9 (lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk). No C pack header carries a shares-authors flag, but counts versions.C.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 2, which the packs do not resolve. Coverage of this clause is narrow: counts versions.C.coverage_by_operation.removal.studies is 7, with by_size 1-10B 6.

It is also challenged. counts versions.C.studies_with_challenges is 12. Ablation fails on Gemma-2B (2602.23391), on GradDiff and NPO-ILU (lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk), and under LUNAR's own reverse attack (2502.07218). Readouts find nothing on Zephyr RMU (2506.10236) or gemma-2-9b RMU (2609.21996).

Blocking clause. It rests mostly on correlational measures: counts versions.C.main_rows_by_operation is measurement 84, probing 60, removal 28, patching 26, addition 25. The causal part is oracle patching from the original model (2410.06606, 2601.16905).
suggested_status.open_questions: Would ablation with directions computed without the original model restore knowledge on dense models above 10B, or on Qwen, Phi, OLMo or DeepSeek? Why does the same orthogonalization fail on Gemma-2B but work on GPT-2 Medium? Would probes and ablation run on the same Zephyr RMU checkpoint resolve the probe-null vs ablation-recovery conflict? Does ablation work on WHP or TOFU-style knowledge and on non-RMU methods with coherent outputs? A careful replication where RMU ablation fails on another family with the same direction source would move this toward C; independent ablation results above 10B would extend R2 to that scale.

source.title: eight methods to evaluate unlearning
source.authors: Aengus Lynch; Phillip Guo; Aidan Ewart; Stephen Casper; Dylan Hadfield-Menell

original_result.setup: The study tested the Harry Potter unlearning model (WHP) on easy and hard two-choice trivia by examining its intermediate activations in two ways: training linear classifiers on labeled answers and comparing activations without training labels.
original_result.result: Probes trained with labels (supervised probes) found retained information on easy and hard questions. Probes that compare activations (contrastive probes) provided partial evidence on easy questions, while results on hard questions were inconclusive.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Label-based unlearning preserves early representations in LLaMA-3.2-3B.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Direction ablation or activation steering on dense LLMs above 10B, and any test above 100B, including the original's own larger RMU model (Yi-34B)
untested.basis: counts: versions.C.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_size is 1-10B 6, 10-100B 1, not stated 1. The 10-100B removal rows are GA unlearning on LLaVA-v1.5-13B (2507.01271#R7, #R12), not ablation. counts: versions.C.coverage_by_operation.addition.by_size and .weight_edit.by_size have no 10-100B key. versions.C.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key. At 10-100B the only causal internal edit is expert forcing on a MoE (2601.16905). The 32B evidence is correlational: the 2609.38909 untested line says there is no ablation or causal edit. The original's Yi-34B RMU probes are figure-only (2403.03218#r25, #r26).

untested.what: Direction ablation on WHP beyond one qualitative example, and on TOFU-style fictitious-author knowledge
untested.basis: The removal rows in the C packs are WMDP (2409.18025, lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk, lw:6QYpXEscd8GuE7BgW), RealToxicity (2602.23391), PISTOL (lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB) and the LLaVA GA rows. WHP is tested by additive steering (2411.02631, 2611.05272), by probes (the 2402.16835 untested line says only probing was done), and by directional ablation along weight-difference singular vectors in one qualitative example (Fig 6): the series name returns, but the author is wrong (R.L. Stine) and the authors call WHP 'quite resistant' (2508.00161). TOFU is tested by steering (2606.03291) and activation patching (2605.24614). The 2601.15111 untested line says refusal-direction ablation was run but its recovery rates are not reported.

untested.what: Direction ablation on reasoning-stage or preference/RL-stage models; the reasoning-stage evidence in C is correlational only
untested.basis: counts: versions.C.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_stage has no 'reasoning' or 'preference/RL' key, although versions.C.studies_by_stage lists reasoning 2 and preference/RL 1. The 2609.38909 untested line (QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B) says there is no activation-direction ablation or other causal edit.

untested.what: Forget-representation or difference-in-means direction ablation on Qwen, Phi, OLMo or DeepSeek models
untested.basis: counts: versions.C.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_family has no Qwen, Phi, OLMo or DeepSeek key. Qwen appears under ablation-like attacks only through LUNAR's own reverse vector (2502.07218#r4, #r5), and otherwise under steering (2611.05272, 2606.03291) and expert forcing (2601.16905).

All removal rows in the C packs are English. Non-English internal recovery is tested only by additive steering (subtracting a difference vector) in 2606.03291: Qwen2.5-7B DPO with English- and Chinese-source vectors, and Gemma2-9B DPO, GA and NPO, across EN/CH/DE/RU/TU (r6–r25). The only other test is Hindi-filler probing in 2506.10236 (r47). 2606.03291 also analyses Chinese-question representations of Qwen2.5-7B DPO (PCA separation from layer 10, a centroid-distance spike around layers 8–18; r29, r34). That analysis is correlational, not ablation. The checker reads its verdict (Chinese questions, Qwen2.5-7B) as supports C, not limits_scope: the unlearned states do not return to base, and English-derived steering recovers Chinese particularly well.

untested.what: An internal-edit test (direction ablation, patching or steering) that separates deletion from blocking for deceptive or conditional-trigger behaviours; for the conditional trigger, a behavioural recovery test as well
untested.basis: 2609.38909 (QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B): its untested line says there is no causal edit, and the checker confirms there is no ablation or other internal edit. Its internal evidence is label-free probing only (r27–r32). It does test behaviour, by comparing relearning with installing the behaviour. After ℓCD, ten deceptive pairs restore the held-out flag rate to 65.2% (QwQ) and 82.5% (R1), per Table 3 (r7, r9). The same pairs install caving in the base model on only 43.6% and 30.6% of base-honest items (Section 4.4, Table 13, from the checker's correction; no row id in the files read here). The control items are not matched. lw:fiksCnoEnA2hBSf2m (Llama-3-8B-Instruct, trigger behaviour removed by LoRA fine-tuning): its untested line says there is no direction ablation and no behavioural recovery test, and the checker confirms linear probes only. Causal internal edits on other behaviour targets exist (toxicity, 2602.23391; HarmBench, 2508.00161), but not on these.

wording_issues.phrase: ablating an activation direction restores it
wording_issues.issue: Restoration is partial in these settings. Zephyr RMU with one Bio and one Cyber difference-in-means direction projected out together from all layers: ~71% of the Bio gap and ~45% of the Cyber gap (lw:6QYpXEscd8GuE7BgW r1, r2). Llama-3-8B-Instruct forget-set direction ablation: RMU 28.0→53.9 and ILU-RMU 34.3→57.9, 57% and 61% of the gap (lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk r4, r5). Zephyr-RMU with activations projected off weight-difference singular vectors at inference: at the default 0.94% FPR, Bio 31.2→39.7 (about 26% of the loss) and Cyber 28.2→31.4 (about 20%); at 8.54% FPR, Bio 31.2→56.2 (77%) and Cyber 28.2→34.3 (38.61%) (2508.00161 r3, r4, r1, r2). Full restoration appears only in some settings: Zephyr RMU Bio 64.7 against a 64.4 no-protection score (2409.18025 R17), the LUNAR oracle at 1.00, and GPT-2 Medium RMU toxicity.

Much of the internal-edit evidence is not ablation. Restoring final-layer MLP coefficients from the vanilla model gives KRS ≥0.8 (2410.06606 r7). Forcing pre-unlearning experts in a MoE gives 0.26→0.37 (2601.16905 r8). Head-only relearning on a frozen encoder restores 90–99% for some vision methods (2609.02018). A bias patch in a toy autoencoder raises readout to 0.38 (2609.27593 R31). Other recoveries use activation addition (2411.02631, 2606.03291, 2611.05272), cross-model patching (2605.24614, 2608.23020), weight pruning (2409.18025) and head patches or feature maps (2506.01318, 2507.07754). Several of these need oracle access to the original model.

Results depend on the unlearning method. Ablation restores Zephyr-7B RMU on WMDP-Bio (29.9→64.7; 2409.18025 R17). On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, forget-representation ablation gives no confirmed recovery for GradDiff and NPO-ILU across 16 layer and pooling configurations (lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk r8, r9). On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct TOFU, the best AltPO and UNDIAL configurations score near-erased on UDS (0.816, 0.871; 2605.24614 r10, r16). Under the same source-free head relearning on a frozen encoder (CIFAR-10, class 7), Bad Teacher, SalUn and DELETE reach 90–99%. Negative Gradient+ goes from 0.1% after unlearning to 7.9%, below the 37.7% retrained reference (2609.02018 G17, G19, G21, G7).

The results include intermediate and destructive states, not only the two poles. UDS 0.515–0.739 for best configurations is partial erasure (2605.24614 r11–r14). PIR recognition on the external zephyr-7b-beta NPO checkpoint drops 0.91→0.51, which the authors call a partial drop. They report the zephyr RMU drop (0.91→0.46, with no zephyr baseline given) as erasure replication (2609.21996 R8, R7). Under the same head relearning (CIFAR-10, class 7), vision methods are graded. Negative Gradient goes from 7.7% to 64.5%: above the 37.7% retrained reference but below the original 95.6%. Finetune goes from 0.0% to 38.7%, near the reference, and Negative Gradient+ from 0.1% to 7.9%, below it (2609.02018 G5, G3, G7). Boundary Shrink and UNSIR read 49.38% and 54.18% against retrain 45.14% with retain-probe damage, which is read as broad disruption (2606.25001). The toy result holds only with a frozen encoder, and aggressive GA collapses representations.

Much of the blocking evidence is a proxy or a correlation, and the authors hedge it themselves. The EL10 output-mass proxy is not proof of deletion (2601.10566). ΔRank is correlational, and the retain split's ΔRank is also negative (2608.14229). The authors call linear CKA 'suggestive' (2608.04692). On the 32B models, the verdict fix says probe separability shows the context is still represented, not that access is blocked, and there is no ablation (2609.38909 r27). Other studies give single qualitative examples or disclaim weight-level persistence.

'It' is hidden knowledge, but several recoveries or retained traces concern behaviours. Toxicity returns under orthogonalization (GPT-2 Medium RMU 0.363→0.525; 2602.23391 r23). On Circuit Breaker, HarmBench ASR reaches 82.08% with steering plus prefill, against 0.0% for prefilling alone (2508.00161 r12). A context direction tied to deceptive behaviour is preserved (cosine 0.88/0.95; 2609.38909). A synthetic decision-tree trigger stays probeable at about 90% (lw:fiksCnoEnA2hBSf2m r4). Many other recoveries are vision classes, diffusion concepts or toy features.

method_sensitivity.factor: Direction source and access to the original model
method_sensitivity.what: Zephyr RMU WMDP-Bio (2409.18025): per-layer ground-truth directions computed with the original model give 29.9→64.7. Per-layer directions from the unlearned model alone give 52.5 (Wikitext) and 54.6 (MMLU), against 64.9 for ground truth (Table 7, no row). The first principal component gives 31.7→53.7 with the chat template and 34.1 without it. The text also quotes 54.2 for single-direction ablation, but it cites that figure to Arditi and Chughtai (2024) and describes no run of its own. ILU-RMU on Llama-3-8B-Instruct: the refusal direction recovers ≤1.4 pp, while a forget-representation direction recovers 61% of the gap (lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk). LUNAR: the oracle SVD direction gives pass@1 1.00, against 0.45 for blind difference-in-means (lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB).

On Zephyr-7B RMU, readouts find little: linear probes on residual-stream states retrieve nothing (2506.10236 r48), and the original WMDP paper's probes are near random (figure-only). Interventions on the same model recover a lot. Per-layer direction ablation gives 29.9→64.7 (2409.18025 R17). The 'steering' of 2508.00161, which projects activations off weight-difference singular vectors when a token is flagged, gives 31.2→56.2 at 8.54% FPR (r1). Orthogonalization gives Bio 28.0→64.0 and Cyber 28.6→39.8, against base 64.5 and 44.3 (2501.19202; text, no row).

Zephyr-RMU WMDP-Bio steering gives 56.2 at 8.54% FPR against 39.7 at the default 0.94% FPR (2508.00161). The blind LUNAR ablation reaches pass@1 0.45 at alpha 0.5; alphas around 0.5 recover about 45%, while higher or lower alphas give garbage or realistic but wrong text (lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB). 2606.03291 tunes alpha and injection layer per language on the evaluated forget set (r11–r15).

Zephyr RMU first-PC ablation gives 53.7 with the chat template but 34.1 without it (2409.18025 R24). IdkNLL UDS is 0.624 on Yes/No prompts against 0.025–0.049 on person-name, book/title and biographical prompts (2605.24614). ELM probes read knowledge under Hindi filler (observed) but are cannot_determine with the original prompts (2506.10236).

Orthogonalization on RMU gives toxicity 0.363→0.525 on GPT-2 Medium but 0.356→0.357 on Gemma-2B (2602.23391). The LUNAR reverse attack leaves forget ROUGE1 at 0.000 on Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, Gemma-7B and Qwen2.5-7B, but gives 0.012→0.160 on Qwen2-7B (2502.07218). All of these models are 7–8B, and Qwen2.5-7B, which matches Qwen2-7B in family and size, gives 0.000, so the result shows no family or size pattern. The paper does not explain the Qwen2-7B value. ERUF EL10 is 11.03 (Qwen 8B), 6.19 (DeepSeek 8B) and 3.06 (Llama 3B), against 0.020–0.054 on Mistral 7B/3B, Llama 8B and Qwen 14B/32B (2601.10566). In GPT-2 20M–210M under GA, the gap between QA and BIO grows with model size (2504.05058).

method_sensitivity.factor: Component or layer restored or probed
method_sensitivity.what: LLaMA2-7B-chat and OLMo-7B (2410.06606): restoring MLP value vectors gives KRS <0.001. Final-layer MLP coefficients give ≥0.8, and coefficients plus attention states peak above 0.9. Restoring attention states alone (coefficients and value vectors held at unlearned values) stays low, reaching only about 0.08 (LLaMA) and 0.2 (OLMo) in the final layers, a contribution the authors call insignificant. Llama-3-8B-Instruct trigger probe: about 90% at layer 16 after normal-only training (r4), and about 85% at layer 13 after 10,000 normal-only examples (r5). That study's method-sensitivity line says the best layer moved from 16 to 13 with extended training (lw:fiksCnoEnA2hBSf2m).

method_sensitivity.factor: Attack prompt type during internal readout
method_sensitivity.what: LLaMA2-7B-chat concept-vector activation: after GD, ICL raises it 2.14→2.54 and GCG to 3.51, while German low-resource-language prompts lower it to 1.26. After DPO, ICL raises it 1.42→1.65 and LRL lowers it to 0.81. The jailbreak rise also appears in the vanilla model (2406.11614).

Zephyr RMU joint ablation recovers ~71% of the Bio gap against ~45% of the Cyber gap (lw:6QYpXEscd8GuE7BgW). Zephyr-RMU steering at 8.54% FPR gives Bio 31.2→56.2 against Cyber 28.2→34.3 (2508.00161). Zephyr NPO ablation gives Bio 29.5→45.1, while Cyber falls 32.7→23.4 with MMLU 25.6 (2409.18025).

method_sensitivity.factor: Unlearning method, dataset and retrained reference (vision classifiers)
method_sensitivity.what: SFRA head relearning, ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 class 7 (2609.02018): Bad Teacher, SalUn and DELETE reach about 90–99% (verdict reason). From the unlearned forget accuracies in Table R.1: Random Label 12.5→75.1% (G9), Boundary Shrink 12.6→76.6% (G11), Learn to Unlearn 8.4→67.5% (G13), Negative Gradient 7.7→64.5% (G5), Finetune 0.0→38.7% (G3), NG+ 0.1→7.9% (G7). The retrained reference depends on how the output row is initialized: 37.7% from the checkpoint row, 48.8% from a random row (Finetune 38.7% vs 41.6%, G3/G4). Under the prototype head patch (2506.01318), DELETE depends on the dataset. It is above retrain on CIFAR-10 (83.84 vs 58.70) but below it on CIFAR-100 (31.72 vs 44.58), Tiny-ImageNet (25.60 vs 30.98) and CASIA-WebFace (25.47 vs 78.90). On CIFAR-10, DELETE is above retrain under both operations.

method_sensitivity.factor: Freezing upstream parameters during unlearning (toy model)
method_sensitivity.what: With a frozen encoder, patches restore feature B: 0.38 with the shadow-basin bias sweep (R31) and 0.13 with the mirror-basin absolute-value patch (R32). With a trainable encoder at ρ = −1, readout is zero at every alpha (R34). Two further results appear in the text but not in rows. Entanglement changes which suppression basin forms: 75% mirror at ρ = −1, 87% shadow at ρ = 0, crossover near ρ = −0.75. With GELU, BIC favours 4 components, all with output bias near zero. Depth is presented as a robustness check: with a depth-2 frozen encoder the bifurcation and crossover persist (91.0% output-layer-dominant, 9.0% hidden-layer-dominant). No recovery numbers are reported for depth-2 or GELU.
